subject: PrivNet: deployability & network gates for on-prem GitOps modules
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@nimblebank.com>, NimbleBank Platform Ops <platform@nimblebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PrivNet: deployability & network gates for on-prem GitOps modules

Hi Rajiv / Platform team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I attached a lightweight deployability checklist for the on-prem GitOps flow and a short proposal for module interface changes that will make air-gapped installs and strict egress customers (like you) much simpler to run and validate.

High level asks from our side:
- Confirm whether the internal RHEL/CentOS images you use can accept our signed artifacts via your internal registry mirror.
- Identify any network egress rules that would block outbound CA bundle fetching (we have a fallback of pre-bundled certs but want to understand the risk).
- Let us know if you need any additional SHA-signed release artifacts for SBOM/provenance checks.

Attachments: privnet-ci-checklist.xlsx (CI gating matrix), privnet-module-interface-proposal.md (diff/notes).

Proposed next step: 30–40min technical sync Thursday to walk PR #432 and outline the minimal changes for your ops runbook. Propose 11/19 10:00am PT — does that work?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@nimblebank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: NimbleBank Platform Ops <platform@nimblebank.com>, Anita Rao <anita.raos@nimblebank.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: PrivNet: deployability & network gates for on-prem GitOps modules

Karthik —

Thanks for the checklist. Quick clarifications from our side before the sync:
1) Air-gap flow: we cannot allow any runtime egress for artifacts; all artifacts must be mirrored internally and signed. Pre-bundled certs are OK but we need edge-case guidance if cert rotation happens mid-deploy.
2) Registry: we use Harbor with signed image policy. Can you emit both OCI and legacy tarball artifacts? Our SRE prefers OCI but procurement may require tarball for archival.
3) Evidence: procurement will want a short proof-pack (MD + signatures) showing your CI gates that produce release artifacts. SOC2 references are helpful.

Also CC'ing Anita (security) — she will join the sync to validate the gating matrix and ask a few questions about audit logs and API call traces.

We can do 11/19 at 10am PT. Please share the GitHub PR link and any WPA (work-product) that we can review in advance.

—Rajiv
Head of Platform Engineering, NimbleBank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@nimblebank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:24:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PrivNet: deployability & network gates for on-prem GitOps modules

Rajiv / Anita —

Appreciate the specifics. Quick notes from the Redwood side after a short internal review:
- Artifacts: we will publish signed OCI refs and produce a tarball bundle as part of the release job (artifact names and signatures included).
- Cert rotation: add a preflight check in the module that validates the bundled certs against a rotation window; we can fail early with a clear remediation step.
- Evidence pack: Karthik and I will prepare a 1–2 page proof pack that maps the CI gates to build artifacts and audit logs for your procurement team.

Internal asks for our sync:
- Laura, can you prepare the proposed Terraform/Helm variable map that keeps the network policy toggles explicit (no implicit egress permissions)?
- Karthik, can you scope a small Ansible role that runs the preflight and optionally seeds the internal registry?

I attached a rough module-contract-diff.patch showing the variable names we're proposing and a draft CI gating matrix spreadsheet. We'll bring these to the call.

Thanks — see you on 11/19 10am PT.

Marissa
Sr. Manager, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv@nimblebank.com>, NimbleBank Platform Ops <platform@nimblebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PrivNet: deployability & network gates for on-prem GitOps modules — plan and action items

Thanks everyone for a productive sync last week. Following up with the mutual action plan and owners (short).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Redwood: produce 1–2 page proof pack (Marissa) / 2026-11-24
- Redwood: push PR that adds explicit terraform var toggles + helm values for network-policy (Laura) / 2026-11-25 (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-infra/pull/432)
- Redwood: Ansible role for registry seeding & preflight (Karthik) / 2026-11-26 — will include smoke checks and cert validation
- NimbleBank: provide sample Harbor mirror creds and any registry retention policies we should adhere to (Rajiv) / 2026-11-24

Notes and risks:
- If cert rotation occurs during deploy we will gate the run and provide a one-click remediation path (seed new cert bundle via Ansible role).
- Auditability: we'll ensure the CI job emits SBOM and a short provenance JSON we can include in the proof pack (attachments in the PR).

Attachments included with this thread: privnet-ci-checklist.xlsx, privnet-module-interface-proposal.md, module-contract-diff.patch.

Links: hubspot deal 5647382, GitHub PR 432, design notes in Confluence.

If that plan looks good, I'll open the PR and assign reviewers.

—Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Integrations
Redwood Inference
